rule.text: If the top 20% of governance artifacts account for more than 60% of citations, a power law is present.

rank_plot.definition: least-squares line of log10(count) on log10(rank), positive counts only, largest first, tied counts on consecutive ranks; exponent implied by the slope = 1 + 1 / |slope|

power_law_fit.form: discrete power law (zeta distribution): p(x) = x^-alpha / zeta(alpha, x_min), with zeta(alpha, x_min) = sum over k >= 0 of (x_min + k)^-alpha

smallest_ks_distance.rule: the listed cut with the smallest Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance

tail_cut.rule: among the listed cuts that keep at least min_tail_for_tail_cut values, the one with the smallest Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance to the fitted power law

definitions.note: All three are distributions on the integers x >= x_min, so their likelihoods are comparable. The lognormal is fitted for x_min = 1 only.
definitions.power_law: discrete power law (zeta distribution): p(x) = x^-alpha / zeta(alpha, x_min), with zeta(alpha, x_min) = sum over k >= 0 of (x_min + k)^-alpha
definitions.exponential: discrete exponential (geometric): p(x) = (1 - q) q^(x - x_min); maximum likelihood gives q = m / (m + 1), m the mean excess over x_min
definitions.lognormal: a lognormal variable rounded up to the next integer: p(x) = Phi((ln x - mu) / sigma) - Phi((ln(x - 1) - mu) / sigma), x >= 1

lognormal_rounded_to_nearest_instead.definition: p(x) = [F(x + 1/2) - F(x - 1/2)] / [1 - F(1/2)], fitted by nested golden-section search

goodness_of_fit.kind: synthetic reference distribution for an observed distance
goodness_of_fit.method: Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance of the recorded counts to their fitted power law, compared with the distances of synthetic power-law samples of the same size, each refitted; x_min is held fixed
goodness_of_fit.rule: a power law is ruled out when p <= 0.1

bootstrap.kind: computed: nonparametric bootstrap of the recorded counts

simulation_all_positive.kind: synthetic: seeded samples from the three fitted families
simulation_all_positive.note: Synthetic samples of 16 positive counts (the number of positive recorded counts). Each generator uses the parameter fitted to the 16 recorded positive counts, rounded to 2 decimals (the exponential keeps the exact mean 414/16). The script checks that the fitted values round to these.

simulation_tail.kind: synthetic: seeded tails above the tail cut
simulation_tail.note: Synthetic tails above the tail cut (x_min = 13). Each generator uses the parameter fitted to the 12 recorded counts of 13 or more (alpha rounded to 2 decimals; the exponential keeps the exact mean 396/12). Sample size 12 is the observed tail; the larger sizes show what more data would buy.

sensitivity.kind: computed: the same fit on two other sets of counts

measured_by_git_grep.what: the latest run without the two hand-entered counts

before_git_grep.what: the same artifacts in the last run before the counts were measured with git grep (hand-typed counts)

goodness_of_fit.kind: synthetic reference distribution for an observed distance, as in goodness_of_fit

negative_controls.kind: results that could be empty by construction, shown next to a case where the same procedure returns something
